title: Perceptions of Dignity in Palliative Care: An In-Depth Qualitative Exploration
abstract: Background: Preserving personal dignity represents a core clinical imperative in end-of-life care. Methods: Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with terminally ill patients and primary caregivers. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied across all transcribed transcripts. Results: Three overarching themes emerged: bodily autonomy, interpersonal attentiveness from clinicians, and continuity of identity. Conclusions: Palliative teams must cultivate relational sensitivity rather than focusing solely on symptom palliation.
